content:
alex: Kicked off the smoke + stress run for the ProspectX POC this morning. Plan executed: 10m smoke at 1-5 RPS, then 50m ramp to 120 RPS, followed by a 10m peak soak at 200 RPS. Two model variants: redwood-base-fp16 and redwood-base-q4f16. Results below.

maria: Nice — can you paste the test config and the main metrics?

alex: Test config (abbreviated):
```bash
# loader: locust based harness
- concurrency: 200 users
- arrival pattern: linear ramp 0->120 rps over 50m
- payload: median prompt 120 tokens, max 512 tokens, average gen length 80 tokens
- model variants: base-fp16, base-q4f16
- runtime: hosted (region: us-west1) with autoscale off, reserved pool=2 GPUs
- batching: continuous batching enabled, target_batch_size=8, max_latency_slo=0.5s
```

kevin: Observations from infra: GPU utilization hit ~88% on the A100s during the 120 RPS plateau. Host CPU spiked to ~75% during peak. Queue depth correlated with p95 spikes (queue depth>18 -> p95 increases). No OOMs.

ops-bot: [deploy-bot] Canary pool: 2 instances -> healthy. Canary checks passed at 09:12 UTC.

alex: Raw numbers (end-to-end generation latency per response):
- base-fp16 (variant A): median 170ms, p95 540ms, p99 920ms, sustained throughput 82 RPS before queueing grew. Errors: 0.6% 5xx spikes during 200 RPS soak.
- base-q4f16 (variant B): median 140ms, p95 360ms, p99 660ms, sustained throughput 110 RPS. Errors: 0.15% 5xx during peak soak.

sam_sales: Those tolerances look decent. ProspectX asked about cost for the POC shape — can you give a rough token-based estimate for sustained 100 RPS and for a 10-minute 200 RPS burst?

alex: Rough cost back-of-envelope using hosted pricing + burst adders:
- 100 RPS sustained (median prompt+gen ~200 tokens -> 20k tokens/min -> ~28.8M tokens/day): ~$1,700/day on hosted (include model usage + infra amortized) — ballpark.
- 10-minute 200 RPS burst: incremental cost ~+$45 (mostly infra scaling + short GPU-hours).
(we should convert with their token mix; will send detailed sheet)

jules: Security check: ProspectX requires SOC2 + customer-managed VPC option for production. For the POC they can use hosted if we sign NDA + data handling addendum. They also pinged about SSO + SCIM.

maria: Noted. For the POC we'll use anonymized prompts and enable request-level logging only for errors. If they escalate to Private, we should estimate Private deployment lead time (~4-6 weeks) and license fee.

kevin: Quick note on tunables that helped: enabling KV prefix caching reduced repeated prefix latency by ~22% in the smoke run. Batching target=8 kept p95 lower; target 16 increased median slightly but hurt p99 under burst. Recommend target_batch_size=8 for POC.

alex: Actionable summary:
- Variant B (q4f16) is the best balance of latency/cost for ProspectX's prompt distribution.
- POC shape: run 2x q4f16 reserved GPUs, target_batch_size=8, KV cache TTL=30m. Expected sustained ~100 RPS with p95 ~380ms.
- If ProspectX needs <300ms p95 we should propose Dedicated (larger reserved pool + tighter batching and GPU pinning).
- Security: proceed with hosted POC under NDA; prepare Private proposal if they require VPC/SOC2.

sam_sales: Great — I'll update the commercial with those numbers and ask for a quick 30-min sync to show the dashboard. Can you attach the detailed logs and the raw locust CSV?

alex: Uploading artifacts to the POC folder now (link pasted in DM). Will also export the locust CSV and a small runbook for repeating the test in Dedicated.

maria: I'll prepare a short one-pager for the AE + prospect showing p95/p99 charts and the recommended config.

kevin: Follow-up engineering note: to reproduce Dedicated numbers we need to disable autoscaling and pin GPUs; I'll schedule a dry-run on the Dedicated staging pool tomorrow morning.

sam_sales: @alex @maria please add the cost sheet and the Private timeline to the thread so I can forward. Prospect wants a decision by EOD Friday. :thumbsup:

alex: Will do. Adding cost spreadsheet and timeline by EOD PT.

jules: I'll prepare security checklist items they asked for (SOC2 attestation link, contact for DPA).

alex: Final quick callouts: median prompt length matters a lot here — if their live distribution has longer gens (200+ tokens) our p95 will shift ~+60-80ms. Recommending sample traffic set from prospect for next run.

maria: Thanks team. We'll reconvene after the Dedicated dry-run and share slides for the Friday decision.

sam_sales: Thanks all — very helpful.
